title: Integrability of Gaussian Hessian products
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $v>0$. If $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and satisfies $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z$, then for every $i,j\in I$ the function
\[z\longmapsto \left(\frac{(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)}{v^2}-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{v}\right)f(z)
\]
is integrable under the product Gaussian measure with independent coordinates of means $c_k$ and variance parameter $v$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: measurable function bounded in absolute value by 1
replaced: Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. For $i,j\in I$, put $H_{ij}(z)=(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is one if $i=j$ and zero otherwise. If $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and $|f|\le1$, then $H_{ij}f$ is $\mu_{c,v}$-integrable for every $i,j\in I$.
